subject: Reserved capacity tenor & price-protection proposal for Aurora Labs
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed price-protection language for Aurora (draft)

Mateo / Marissa,

Putting a short draft together for Aurora Labs (HL-2309). They want reserved capacity for a sustained period but are worried about GPU market swings — specifically the risk that a long commit could lock them into paying above-market if NVIDIA spot/contract pricing falls.

High level I suggest we offer 3 candidate structures for commercial to take into negotiation:
- Flat-tier discount (simple): 24-month fixed term, fixed discount over list, no indexation. Easier for ops but riskier for customer if prices fall.
- Indexed collar (preferred): 18-month term indexed to a published GPU cost reference with a floor and ceiling (caps the upside and downside).
- Step-up + renewal trigger: 12-month initial term with conditional step-up to longer tenor if utilization thresholds met; allows shorter initial exposure.

Sizing note (ballpark): they asked for sustained 12 A100-equivalent GPUs with 50% burst headroom during product launches. That maps to an 18-month reserved pool of ~16 A100-equivalents with a 4x burst bucket.

Attached: hl-helio-draft-terms.pdf (very rough).

Ask: Mateo — can you validate the sizing / burst assumptions? Marissa — please flag which of these options we can sign off on without exec approval and which need VP/Exec sign-off. I want to get a clear counter to procurement by EOD if possible.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:03:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed price-protection language for Aurora (draft)

Dylan — thanks, saw the notes. Quick technical validation on sizing and ops impact below.

Sizing summary (conservative):
- Baseline reserved pool: 16 A100-equivalents
- Burst policy: 4 additional spot-backed instances (auto-burst) with 30s ramp for warm KV cache
- Expected average utilization: 55-70% steady-state; peaks 95% during launches (2-3 days / quarter)
- KV cache warmup cost: small but non-zero; recommend provisioning a persistent minimal cache per service to reduce regen load.

Operational constraints:
- Indexation clause requires legal to allow us to reference an external published index; if the index is vendor-owned we may need a fallback manual recalculation path.
- Any cap/floor means we must plan for the higher bound in capacity procurement (finance will insist).

I attached a quick runbook: sizing-runbook.xlsx (detailed assumptions & cost calc).

My preference is the indexed-collar at 18 months with a modest floor (3%) and ceiling (12%) — gives Aurora downside protection while limiting Redwood's exposure. If procurement balks at an 18-month lock, suggest we offer a 12 -> auto-roll 6-month trigger based on usage.

Ben — tagging you for a finance read on headroom and approval thresholds. Marissa — can you confirm approval path and whether the indexed option requires Exec sign-off?

Mateo

--
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
From: Procurement Aurora Labs <procurement@auroralabs.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@auroralabs.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 13:21:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tenor & price-protection proposal for Aurora Labs

Mateo — thanks for the quick update and the options. A few clarifying points from Aurora Procurement / Finance:

- We are open to an indexed solution but need a hard cap on increases. Aurora cannot accept open-ended price escalations tied to vendor indices without a maximum annual delta.
- Preferred structure: 12–18 month commit with an annual cap of ~10% on price movement from the start rate, or alternatively a collar where Aurora is protected from >8% upside and still participates in downside up to -3%.
- We cannot accept a mechanism that requires us to co-fund future GPU purchases or hedge costs on your balance sheet.
- If legal insists on referencing an external NVIDIA spot index, we need a fallback published source and explicit calculation examples in the contract.

Attaching our Q forecast so you can see seasonality: aurora-qtr-forecast.csv

Can your team share concrete pricing scenarios (numbers) for both the flat-tier and an indexed-collar so we can model cashflow? Also please state any internal approval thresholds that would delay signing.

Best,
J. Procurement (on behalf of Aurora Labs)
procurement@auroralabs.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aurora Labs Procurement <procurement@auroralabs.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tenor & price-protection proposal for Aurora Labs

Thanks for the details, team — internal finance view and approval path below.

Pricing scenarios (illustrative, all $ figures monthly equivalent):
- Option A (Flat 24m): 35% discount off list, monthly $98k, requires Director FP&A approval (sub-$500k ARR exposure).
- Option B (Indexed collar, 18m): start monthly $112k, index to NVIDIA public index, floor -3% / cap +12% annual, requires VP Finance sign-off (>$500k exposure).
- Option C (Step-up 12->24m trigger): start $105k for 12m then reassess; requires VP Finance + Head of Revenue for roll to 24m.

Approval thresholds: any net present exposure > $750k or multi-year legal credit terms require Exec Finance & CRO approval. Indexed collars are operationally fine but increase headroom planning; finance will require a contingency buffer equal to the ceiling for capital planning.

We can prepare a side-by-side cashflow model; see pricing-scenarios-v3.pdf (attached). To move quickly we can provision a draft commercial term sheet with the indexed collar + 9% cap / 3% floor as a starting point — that would likely sit under VP approval. If Aurora requests a tighter cap (<=8%) we will need Exec sign-off.

Let me know which cap/floor pair Aurora prefers and we will push an exec read for sign-off if necessary.

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Aurora Labs <procurement@auroralabs.com>, Lina Park <lina.park@auroralabs.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 18:05:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tenor & price-protection proposal for Aurora Labs

Aurora — appreciate the constructive feedback. Based on internal discussion here's a counter-proposal for quick alignment:

- Term: 18 months (auto-renew opt-in at month 15).
- Capacity: 16 A100-equivalents reserved, with a planned 4-instance burst pool.
- Pricing protection: Indexed collar linked to the public NVIDIA cloud index, floor = -3% / cap = +9% annual.
- Onboarding: one-time $50k credit to offset initial cache warmup & integration cost.
- Approval: VP Finance sign-off required; we will route for approval immediately once Aurora confirms intent to proceed (target response by 2027-11-09).

If Aurora can accept the 9% cap we can lock terms into a draft term sheet and share a marked contract for legal redlines next week. If you need tighter cap we will escalate for Exec approval which will add ~3 business days.

Next step: Aurora confirmation on cap/floor preference and commitment timeline.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com
